delete_diff: No matching layer exists. TRANSFER.C compiles independently with normal TC2.0. The bridge only adapts the original boundary; clean C owns arithmetic, conditions, ordered writes and transfer progress.

differences.finding: Sequential biased store followed by conditional delayed copies; earlier stores may change later source words, selector or cursor. Volatile native C preserves these accesses; synthetic alias tests agree.

Explicit far source/output pointers, near DS cursor/selection views and far private progress result. Result fields preserve historical AX/DI/ES and conditional BX/SI outputs without putting copying or selection semantics into the shim.
TC2.0 replaces LODS/STOS with indexed MOV, uses SI for the transferred word, a BP frame and two local slots. Four-byte pointer marshalling and progress stores dominate expansion.
Two original calls with RETs become one C function with two optional transfer blocks and a shared epilogue. Six-byte far-call/NOP gate preserves continuation9BE8.
Original arithmetic flags at9BE8 are dead at the next CMP; all control flags preserved and all flags compared after that original instruction.
No platform operations in body. DOS near/far addressing and stack model remain explicit; no portable ISO C claim.

Known decoded inbound graph only; no proof against unresolved indirect entry. Arbitrary asynchronous mutation and timing not covered. Extra64-byte stack reservation is a precondition, not globally proven capacity.

recommendation: Verified C is preferable to prescribing the original register/string-op choreography. The101-byte bridge exceeds the77-byte original cluster. A larger boundary or proven dead outputs may reduce adaptation cost; do not generalize a matching DSL.
